title: Interned string table slot lookup and insertion
summary: Recovered Game.exe 0x4f0d10 (RVA 0xf0d10), 99 bytes, as a readable State member. Selects a 20-byte node using string hash at +8 and table exponent at +7, follows next pointers, requires key tag 4 and interned pointer equality, preserves existing nil-valued slots, and delegates missing keys as a temporary tagged string to the accepted new-key helper. Preserves the original absolute nil-sentinel comparison. No table cache invalidation is performed. Original custom calling convention is ECX=state, EDX=table, stack string pointer with caller cleanup and EAX return; test-only GCC regparm(3) with dummy EAX models that convention. Observed callers at 0x4f6443, 0x4f6e06 and 0x557135 pop the string argument and inspect returned value tag. All three linked accepted reference spans were independently byte-checked against immutable Game.exe; original four-entry dispatch data was also verified. GCC behavioral tests passed and pinned MSVC2013 compiled impl.cpp under O1, O2 and O2 /Oy-. No matching credit claimed.
test_description: 55,296 direct original lookup comparisons cover every exponent byte 0..255 (x86 shift masking), hashes 0..7, direct and three-node chained matches, same-pointer wrong-tag rejection, equal-hash different-pointer rejection, and value tags 0..8 including nil. Return pointers and entire guarded fixtures are compared, including all table fields, node payloads/links, strings, array, state and GC global storage; existing lookups must leave every byte unchanged. Another 24 locally mapped original insertion comparisons cover vacant main bucket, collision linking and displaced-occupant relocation with black/nonblack tables and all key white-bit combinations. Independent assertions check key copy, nil value preservation, lastFree, link relocation, unchanged cache byte and conditional GC grayagain effects. Three controlled dependency-boundary checks verify state/table/string/tag forwarding, exactly one call, unchanged fixture and result/null/sentinel passthrough. Tests explicitly initialize test-owned FS backing, require successful test_install_fs and verify FS head restoration after original calls. Full local insertion execution maps the 16-byte non-executable .oracle_dispatch at 0x4f018c. Both full mapped and reduced unmapped runs passed. An unmapped trusted run explicitly reports skipped insertion comparisons while retaining all 55,296 direct original lookup cases and controlled miss checks.
known_limits: Only the assigned routine is recovered; new-key allocation, rehash, GC barrier and main-bucket policy remain explicit VM Services dependencies. Accepted helpers are used without reconstructing them.

Original insertion paths require external dispatch data at 0x4f018c, not part of the accepted main-bucket span or coordinator-guaranteed mappings. Local tests supply and verify it; trusted runs without that mapping explicitly report reduced original coverage.
Full-table rehash, allocator failure, dummy-node empty-table insertion, VM errors and actual GC execution are outside tested paths. No allocation or error policy is invented.

The unusual case where a matched node itself occupies absolute nil sentinel address 0x99a41c is preserved in source but not executed. Corrupt or cyclic chains, invalid objects and concurrent mutation remain outside the original valid-object contract.

The portable member uses an explicit Services argument rather than replacing the custom original register ABI directly. Absolute nil sentinel identity requires translation when integrating a relocated Linux VM.

Pointer-layout assertions describe the original 32-bit VM. No 64-bit binary ABI compatibility, byte-identical C++ rebuild or whole-game equivalence is claimed. The target does not itself use Windows SEH; FS setup validates only normal-path head preservation.
